**Fresh-pass finding: no new evidence, EXP-646 hold plan remains correct.** The 2026-07-01 integrated EXP-646 (monitor/analyst/expansions/EXP-646-pred-field-2026q2-verdict-hold.json) established our_verdict=pending with a scheduled re-check on 2026-08-15 against INTERMAGNET TTB (Tatuoca) quasi-definitive Q2 2026 data. As of 2026-07-14 (d=14 past window close), the Q2 quasi-definitive data has not yet published — INTERMAGNET's typical publication lag for quasi-definitive data is ~90 days after quarter-end, placing Q2 2026 quasi-definitive release in late September 2026 (data/predictions.json:PRED-FIELD-2026Q2 detail_reasoning). Provisional real-time data for April-June 2026 is available, but per EXP-646's Data-Availability Timeline section, provisional data undergoes baseline-drift corrections that can shift F by several nT during the ~45-day post-quarter-end settlement window. That settlement window ends ~2026-08-15, which is precisely why EXP-646 chose that date as the re-check trigger.

**Attempted pull.** A direct HTTP fetch against https://intermagnet.org/data_download.html returned HTTP 200 but the download workflow is session/GUI-driven and does not expose a scriptable endpoint for per-station monthly-mean extraction in this analyst environment (verification-attempt log this run). No usable numerical Jan-2026 or Jun-2026 F-component figure was obtainable that would pass the 'defensible measurement' bar. Attempting to compute ΔF from unsettled provisional data ~14 days after quarter-end would produce a verdict driven more by baseline-drift artifact than by real secular variation — this is exactly the failure mode EXP-646's 45-day settlement window was designed to avoid (monitor/analyst/expansions/EXP-646-pred-field-2026q2-verdict-hold.json Data-Availability Timeline).

**Kernel of truth (unchanged from EXP-646).** The dome correctly identifies that (a) TTB sits in the SAA region, (b) SAA total-field intensity IS decaying, (c) the direction of change (weakening) matches mainstream core-dynamo theory, and (d) the 35 nT threshold is a real, testable magnitude — the dome deserves credit for committing to a falsifiable number rather than a directional-only hedge. The failure mode is well-understood: 35 nT / 6 months annualises to ~70 nT/year, which is 2-2.8x the CHAOS-7/IGRF-14 western-cell secular-variation rate at TTB (~25-35 nT/year per Finlay et al. 2020, https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s40623-020-01252-9). The prediction is structurally the same magnitude-overshoot pattern that took PRED-073 down at d=4 (data/predictions.json:PRED-073).

This is a mechanical transition that reflects dome-side silence, not a scientific verdict. The dome page still shows PENDING with no result posted and no manual commit since 2026-04-17 (d=88 drought at time of this poll). The decider should apply the pending -> dome_silent field update on data/predictions.json:PRED-FIELD-2026Q2.author_status as part of resolving ISS-2972. Next mechanical transition (dome_silent_terminal at d=30 = 2026-07-30) will be handled by a separate poller-triaged issue.

**Our_verdict remains pending per EXP-646 plan.** No amendment. The 2026-08-15 re-check date and the verdict rule (four-case decision tree in EXP-646 detail_reasoning) remain the correct trigger and procedure. When 2026-08-15 arrives, the analyst pulls TTB F-component monthly means for Jan 2026 and Jun 2026, computes ΔF = F_Jan − F_Jun, and applies the rule (monitor/analyst/expansions/EXP-646-pred-field-2026q2-verdict-hold.json Verdict rule at re-check). If provisional data on 2026-08-15 remains too noisy, defer to 2026-10-01 (post-Q2 quasi-definitive release) per EXP-646's contingency clause.

**Resolution recommendation for ISS-2972.** Close as OBE / covered-by-existing-EXP with pointer to EXP-646. The poller-triaged fresh-pass request is discharged: the analytical position was already correct as of 2026-07-01, and 14 days of dome silence do not change the verdict rule — they only trigger the mechanical author_status transition, which is separately routed. No content change to data/predictions.json is needed beyond the author_status field update.
